title: CAP Endometrium — Histologic Type
text: Endometrial carcinoma histologic typing (CAP/WHO-aligned). Common types: endometrioid carcinoma (glandular architecture, often squamous morules); serous carcinoma (marked nuclear atypia, papillary or solid growth, p53 abnormal in most); clear cell carcinoma (hobnail cells, clear or eosinophilic cytoplasm, hyaline stroma); mucinous carcinoma (>50% mucinous cells); carcinosarcoma (malignant epithelial and mesenchymal components). Endometrioid subtypes may show villoglandular or secretory patterns. POLE-ultramutated, mismatch repair-deficient, and p53-mutant (NSMP) profiles are reportable molecular categories for endometrioid-type tumors. Mixed carcinomas: report types and approximate percentages when two or more types are present.

title: CAP Endometrium — FIGO Grade
text: FIGO grading of endometrioid endometrial carcinoma is based on solid non-squamous (non-morular) growth. Grade 1: 5% or less solid growth. Grade 2: 6–50% solid growth. Grade 3: more than 50% solid growth. Squamous differentiation and morules do not count toward the solid component. Serous, clear cell, and most non-endometrioid types are considered high grade by definition (FIGO grade 3 equivalent) regardless of architecture. Assess solid areas on H&E at intermediate magnification; correlate with cytologic atypia when borderline.

title: CAP Endometrium — Myometrial Invasion
text: Depth of myometrial invasion is measured from the endomyometrial junction to the deepest point of invasion. The endomyometrial junction is often irregular; look for compressed non-neoplastic endometrial glands adjacent to or at the base of the tumor. Carcinoma involving adenomyosis without destructive stromal invasion should not be counted as myometrial invasion. Report depth in millimeters and as a percentage of myometrial thickness when possible. FIGO stage IA subdivisions use depth and/or percentage thresholds. Extensive sampling is required when preoperative biopsy showed carcinoma but no gross lesion is visible.

title: CAP Endometrium — Lymphovascular Invasion
text: Lymphovascular invasion (LVSI) is defined as tumor cells within endothelial-lined spaces. Distinguish true LVSI from retraction artifact (smooth contour, conforms to space, no endothelial lining). Report LVSI as present or absent; some protocols request focal versus extensive involvement. LVSI supports staging and prognosis but is distinct from myometrial invasion depth. Correlate with peritumoral lymphatic-rich stroma at 20x; use endothelial markers (e.g. CD31, D2-40) when morphology is equivocal.

title: WHO 2020 — Hyperplasia and AH/EIN
text: WHO two-tier endometrial precancer classification. Hyperplasia without atypia: increased gland-to-stroma ratio with tubular, branching, or cystically dilated glands; uniform cytology across the specimen; benign, often regresses with progestin. Atypical hyperplasia / endometrial intraepithelial neoplasia (AH/EIN): crowded glands plus cytologic alteration distinct from background endometrium (nuclear enlargement, loss of polarity, vesicular chromatin, prominent nucleoli). Essential criteria are architectural crowding and cytologic change relative to background. Desirable supportive criteria include loss of PTEN, PAX2, or mismatch repair protein expression. AH/EIN carries significant risk of concurrent or subsequent endometrioid carcinoma.

title: CAP Uterine Sarcoma — Spindle LMS Criteria
text: Conventional (spindle cell) uterine leiomyosarcoma requires two of three features: (1) coagulative tumor cell necrosis, (2) marked cytologic atypia, (3) mitotic activity at or above threshold (commonly 10 mitoses per 10 HPF in 0.55 mm field, or 4 mitoses per mm2). Leiomyoma and STUMP lack the full combination. Necrosis must be coagulative tumor cell necrosis, not hyaline or infarct-type necrosis common in benign leiomyomas. Immunohistochemistry: desmin, h-caldesmon, SMA often positive; use panel when smooth muscle differentiation is subtle.

title: CAP Uterine Sarcoma — Epithelioid and Myxoid LMS
text: Epithelioid leiomyosarcoma: predominantly round or polygonal cells, nested or corded growth; may show mild atypia; diagnose with moderate-to-severe atypia, tumor cell necrosis, or elevated mitoses (lower threshold than spindle LMS in many cases). Myxoid leiomyosarcoma: abundant myxoid stroma, often hypocellular; any degree of cytologic atypia, tumor cell necrosis, or more than 1 mitosis per 10 HPF may suffice. Infiltrative borders support malignancy when cytology is deceptively bland. Extensive sampling is required in myxoid tumors to find diagnostic foci.

title: Endometrial Cycle Phase Morphology
text: Proliferative phase: tubular glands with pseudostratified nuclei, mitoses in glands and stroma, relatively dense stroma, straight or slightly tortuous glands. Early secretory (days 16–19): subnuclear vacuoles in glands, increasing stromal edema. Mid secretory: maximal stromal edema, tortuous glands with serrated lumina, secretion in gland lumina. Late secretory/decidual: stromal predecidua, exhausted glands. Menstrual endometrium: glandular breakdown, stromal collapse, hemorrhage, neutrophils. Dating requires correlation of glands and stroma; inflammation can obscure phase assessment.

title: Chronic Endometritis — Histologic Criteria
text: Chronic endometritis is defined by stromal plasma cell infiltration. Morphologic clues: superficial stromal edema, gland-stromal dyssynchrony, increased stromal cellularity, lymphoid aggregates. Plasma cells have eccentric nuclei, clock-face chromatin, and perinuclear hof; distinguish from stromal fibroblasts and lymphocytes. CD138 immunostain improves sensitivity when H&E is equivocal. Diagnosis is easier in proliferative-phase biopsies; secretory stromal edema can mask plasma cells. Acute endometritis shows neutrophils in epithelium and stroma, often with breakdown.

title: Endometrial Stromal Sarcoma vs Smooth Muscle Tumors
text: Low-grade endometrial stromal sarcoma (LG-ESS): tongue-like myometrial infiltration, cells resemble proliferative-phase endometrial stroma, often CD10 positive, may show sex-cord or smooth muscle differentiation. High-grade ESS and undifferentiated uterine sarcoma show greater atypia and mitotic activity. Distinction from cellular leiomyoma: ESS has characteristic vascular pattern (spiral arteriole-like vessels) and less fascicular smooth muscle architecture. Uterine tumor resembling ovarian sex cord tumor (UTROSCT) is a separate entity with variable immunoprofile.

title: Glandular and Papillary Patterns in Uterine Neoplasms
text: Glandular pattern: endometrioid carcinoma (back-to-back glands, cribriforming), adenocarcinoma variants. Papillary pattern: serous carcinoma (complex papillae with stratified atypical cells), villoglandular endometrioid variant (milder atypia, long slender papillae). Solid pattern: sheets of cells without gland formation; counts toward FIGO grade in endometrioid tumors. Spindle pattern: smooth muscle tumors, carcinosarcoma mesenchymal component, metaplastic carcinoma. Clear cell and secretory patterns have distinct cytoplasmic features. Pattern assessment guides subtype and grade.

title: FIGO Endometrial Carcinoma Stage (Pathologic)
text: Pathologic staging integrates depth of myometrial invasion, cervical stromal involvement, adnexal spread, peritoneal involvement, and nodal status. Stage I: confined to corpus. IA: limited invasion (depth/percentage thresholds per FIGO edition). IB: deeper invasion. II: cervical stromal invasion. III: local/regional spread including adnexa, vagina, parametrium, or positive pelvic nodes. IV: bladder/bowel mucosa or distant metastasis. Report correlates gross findings, microscopic invasion depth, LVSI, and nodal pathology. Serosa involvement and parametrial extension require careful gross and microscopic correlation.
